answers.Q1:
Linked List - A linked list is a linear data structure in which elements, called Nodes, are stored in non-contiguous memory locations. Each node contains two parts: data and a pointer (link) to the next node in the sequence.

Features: Store nodes in non-contiguous memory. Dynamic size. Easy insertion etc.

Hence, Array provides fast access to elements, & linked list offers dynamic memory allocation.

) Array - An Array is a linear data structure that stores a collection of elements of the same data type in contiguous memory locations. Each element is identified by its index, allowing direct and fast access to data.

Features of Array - Store homogeneous data. Elements are stored in contiguous memory. Support direct access using a index.

② Space complexity - Space complexity measure the amount of memory measured by an Algorithm during its execution. It includes memory used for variables, data structures, and temporary storage.

Therefore, complexity analysis is used to evaluate the efficiency of Algorithms.
